attacks.challenge: 256 MiB/context may itself make a specialist uneconomic
attacks.evidence: 36GB HBM3E holds 134 frozen contexts; reported market memory cost per context is low relative to complete-system fairness thresholds

attacks.challenge: DP6 logical traffic may make modern HBM bandwidth insufficient
attacks.evidence: >1.2 TB/s leaves attacker-favorable bandwidth-only upper ceilings about 1.46k-2.17k work/s before random-access/compute penalties

attacks.challenge: dependent latency may close the economics by itself
attacks.evidence: capacity-latency sensitivity remains hundreds of work/s over a wide latency range; complete W/$ determine whether 3x/5x is crossed

attacks.challenge: bank/interleave locality may create a hidden specialized shortcut
attacks.evidence: prior exact-trace stress found no material generic exploit in modeled mapping family

attacks.challenge: current HBM price inflation may itself make the attack uneconomic
attacks.evidence: market prices are incomplete and do not bound logic/package/NRE; even high memory price cannot be promoted to complete-system LCVW

attacks.challenge: advanced-node design cost necessarily protects DP6
attacks.evidence: industry averages are volume- and design-dependent sensitivities, not transferable DP6 ASIC lower bounds

attacks.challenge: One Machine can infer complete specialist work/W and work/USD from component data
attacks.evidence: exact-path sustained throughput, whole-system W and all-in cost remain first-order external discriminants
